History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute dizziness with spinning sensation, unsteadiness, and ear buzzing (vertigo). Nausea reported. No fever. No ear pain or discharge. Hearing described as intact. Symptoms started ~2 hours ago while preparing breakfast; continuous since onset. Similar episode about one month ago that resolved within 5–10 minutes.
- Context: Patient notes room feels like it is moving; unable to walk straight but legs/arms are functioning.
- Associated/negative findings: No recent viral illness; no reported weakness of limbs; no muffled hearing beyond buzzing; no current vomiting mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- Premature ovarian failure; has taken hormone replacement therapy (HRT). 
- Allergies: None.
- Medications: HRT (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Physical Examination:
- Patient-reported findings: Vertigo with persistent spinning sensation; unsteady gait; ears buzzing; no ear discharge; no focal limb weakness; no fever; hearing described as intact.
- No additional objective findings documented (vital signs not provided; no other exam findings recorded).

Impression:
- Labyrinthitis suspected (acute vestibular syndrome) with ongoing vertigo and nausea.

Management Plan:
- Prescription provided (drug name not specified in transcript): 1 tablet three times daily for 10 days. Route/further details not documented. Pickup through Cross Pharmacy/Lloyd Pharmacy in system.
- Symptomatic relief discussed; paracetamol mentioned as an example of symptomatic relief if fever develops.
- Plan to have patient seen by a doctor for an ear examination to assess middle ear status.
- Ongoing assessment: blood pressure and gait/walk analysis planned during waiting period.
- Red flags for urgent care: new weakness of legs/arms, sudden severe headache, or violently worsened symptoms; if these occur, go to A&E.
- Follow-up: appointment with a clinician to examine ears and determine next steps; patient instructed to call support to book the appointment.

Patient Summary:
- A patient with acute vertigo and dizziness, likely labyrinthitis, with associated nausea and aural buzzing. Previous similar episode. On HRT for premature ovarian failure. A symptomatic medication was prescribed, and the patient will have an in-person ear examination and follow-up with a clinician; advised to seek urgent care if red flags develop.

Key Takeaways:
- Suspected labyrinthitis presenting with acute vertigo and ongoing unsteadiness; arrange ENT-ear examination.
- Take the prescribed tablet (1 tablet three times daily for 10 days) and seek follow-up with a clinician.
- Monitor for red-flag symptoms (new limb weakness, severe headache, violent vomiting); seek emergency care if they occur.

Next Steps:
- Ear examination by a clinician to evaluate middle/inner ear status.
- Complete vitals assessment (BP, etc.) and gait assessment during waiting period.
- Schedule and attend follow-up appointment with a doctor.
- If symptoms worsen or new alarming symptoms develop, go to A&E.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation beyond HRT; no complete list of current medications or over-the-counter agents.
  - Social history (smoking, alcohol, occupational factors) not documented.
  - No explicit documentation of allergies beyond “None.”
  - No confirmed drug name for the prescribed medication; only dosing provided.
- Conflicts:
  - PMH documented as “premature ovarian failure” by patient; clinician’s transcript notes “premature hearing failure” in one line—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall coherent with a minor transcription error regarding PMH; some details (exact drug name) not specified in the transcript.
